evidence.curator_note: GENERIC SCHEME, printed under the heading 'EE+'. The book draws a ring of unspecified size that contains the heteroatom Y at the top; Y carries the + charge, is single-bonded to one ring carbon and DOUBLE-bonded to the neighbouring ring carbon, which bears the substituent R (a cyclic onium / oxocarbenium ion). The reaction arrow is labelled 'i, i' = two successive charge-site (inductive) cleavages. Products: the linear onium ion R-C(triple bond)Y+ (an acylium for Y=O) plus a CYCLIC neutral (drawn as the closed 'half-moon' D-shape, i.e. a carbocycle, not a chain). INSTANTIATION (convention F/B): Y=O, R=CH3, ring size 6 (the same hexagon the book draws explicitly one line lower in Eq 8.52), giving the 2-methyl-oxocarbenium of tetrahydropyran, C6H11O+ m/z 99.0804; the charge is localised on the ring oxygen in the mapped SMILES exactly where the book prints the '+'. Products for that instantiation: acetylium CH3-C#O+ (m/z 43.0178) + cyclobutane. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are both drawn full-headed (two-electron) arcs and no implicit move is needed - this EE+ path is entirely heterolytic, so the electron bookkeeping closes with the two drawn arrows alone. Arc 1 (left) leaves the Y-C sigma bond and points into the ring cavity: that pair becomes the new C-C bond that closes the neutral carbocycle (maps 4-7). Arc 2 (right) leaves the ring C-C bond next to the substituted carbon and points up at the Y=C bond, raising it to Y#C+ (maps 1-2).
